decisive_items: Frontal nerve biopsy: Cross section of nerve showing malignant cells with mitotic activity
response.rationale: Desmoplastic melanoma is strongly supported by the recurring forehead lesion with extensive perineural/intraneural invasion, a hallmark feature, and the biopsy confirming malignant melanoma within a nerve. R6 describes the same process but is less specific as a standalone diagnosis, while R5 is too broad and R1 implies metastasis not supported by local spread.

rejected.why: Metastatic melanoma is not supported; the lesion is locally recurrent with perineural spread, not distant metastasis.
Cavernous sinus syndrome is an anatomical description, not the underlying diagnosis; the mass extends to the cavernous sinus but the cause is melanoma.
Orbital apex syndrome is a clinical syndrome, not the etiologic diagnosis; the findings are due to melanoma invasion.
Malignant melanoma is too general; the specific subtype with prominent perineural invasion is desmoplastic melanoma.
